sentences.text: Comahuesuchus was an extinct notosuchian crocodylomorph that lived in Argentina during the late Cretaceous.
The type species C. brachybuccalis was a small animal.
Its skull morphology makes Comahuesuchus an unusual crocodylomorph, distinguished by an extremely short and wide snout.
Its dentition was reduced but included two pairs of canine-like teeth.
The genus Comahuesuchus was described by the paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1991.
José Bonaparte created the monotypic family Comahuesuchidae within Notosuchia when he described the genus.
Research suggests that Comahuesuchus is more closely related to Mariliasuchus amarali than to other notosuchians.
A second species, C. bonapartei, was assigned to the genus in 2023 based on fossils from the Sierra Barrosa and Portezuelo Formations.
Fossils of Comahuesuchus date from the Turonian to Santonian stages, between 93.9 and 83.6 million years ago.
It is debated whether Anatosuchus minor belongs to the Comahuesuchidae family, as some analyses suggest it does not.
